items.headline: Straiker's $64M agent-security round and the Claude Cowork sandbox escape
items.diff_narrative: This is a fresh thread today. Yesterday's lead was regulatory (China's anthropomorphic-AI rules forcing Doubao and Qwen to switch off user-created agents); today the agent-security angle flips from policy to attack surface and defensive market. Straiker's $64M Series A (total $85M, Discover/Ascend/Defend product line, 15x run-rate growth) lands the same week Armadin published a full sandbox-escape chain in Anthropic's Claude Cowork, reaching root inside the isolated Ubuntu VM by abusing a resume flag that skips unprivileged-user creation and a domain-override that disables the network allowlist. Anthropic patched on June 30 while disputing it counts as a security issue. Nothing about funded agent-runtime defense or the Cowork exploit appeared yesterday.

items.headline: Raja Koduri's Oxmiq raises $35M to license an AI GPU architecture, adds Jim Keller
items.diff_narrative: New today, and a distinct move within the non-NVIDIA silicon story that yesterday was carried by Etched. Where Etched sells a finished transformer-only inference ASIC, Oxmiq's $35M Series A (total $60M; Samsung Catalyst Fund, MediaTek, Pegatron, others) commercializes OxCore, a licensable GPU architecture fusing graphics, CPU, and tensor roles into one design, positioned as the Arm of the AI-silicon era. Jim Keller joining the board is the credibility signal. The framing shifts the competitive layer upstream from parts to the IP itself, which yesterday's Etched item did not touch.

items.headline: Unsloth ships DeepSeek-V4 fine-tuning as the model exits preview
items.diff_narrative: New today; the open-weight tuning-stack thread did not appear yesterday. Unsloth's July 7 Studio build adds DeepSeek-V4 support with all reasoning levels, alongside GLM-5.2 and MiniMax-M3, timed to DeepSeek-V4's move from its April MIT-licensed preview toward an official mid-July release (1.6T-parameter MoE, ~49B active, one-million-token context, plus a 284B sibling). With SGLang and vLLM endorsed for serving, the point today is that the download-tune-serve loop for a frontier-tier Chinese open model is now a same-week off-the-shelf pipeline.

items.headline: OpenAI ships gpt-realtime-2.1 and previews a three-tier GPT-5.6 lineup
items.diff_narrative: New today; no OpenAI model-release thread ran yesterday. gpt-realtime-2.1 and gpt-realtime-2.1-mini (July 6) advertise at least 25 percent lower p95 latency plus better alphanumeric recognition and interruption handling, and a limited GPT-5.6 preview (Sol, Terra, Luna tiers at $5/$30, $2.50/$15, $1/$6 per million tokens) went to trusted partners. The emphasis is on the latency-and-price axis for voice agents and enterprise deployment rather than raw capability, a direct contrast to yesterday's regulatory and hardware framing.

items.headline: AI events calendar: ICML Seoul now mid-run, UN Geneva talks converging, fall tracks stacked
items.diff_narrative: The events section carries over from yesterday and remains the one durable thread, but with real state-changes rather than a hold. ICML has moved from yesterday's opening tutorial-and-expo day to the main conference underway July 7-9 (workshops July 10-11), and the July 8 AI Tinkerers SF meetup is now tomorrow rather than later this week. Today also adds the UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance convening all 193 member states in Geneva July 6-7 alongside the ITU AI for Good summit, with the new Independent International Scientific Panel presenting a preliminary report, none of which was in yesterday's list. The standing fall calendar (Hot Chips Aug 23-25, AI Risk Summit Aug 11-12, Ai4 Aug 4-6, AWS re:Invent, GitHub Universe) is unchanged.

items.headline: ICML 2026 in Seoul
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday ICML was a standalone lead story built around its opening: record 23,918 submissions, 6,352 accepted, agent-safety as the dominant theme, and watermark-based reviewer policing that flagged 398 reviewers and triggered 497 desk rejections. Today it is no longer a dedicated section and appears only folded into the events calendar as an in-progress catalyst (main conference July 7-9, program readable through July 11). The submission-pile and reviewer-policing detail dropped out; the item narrowed from a research-frontier feature to a plan-around-it scheduling reference.
